correctness.rationale: The drift is Hurwitz for every finite N with positive damping. Expanding the nilpotent shift in the stationary covariance convolution and integrating t^(2q+d) exp(-2κt) gives the exact binomial sum with D/κ, consistent with the Lyapunov boundary recursion and N=1. For q/N in [ε,1] and d=O(sqrt(N)), the uniform centered-binomial Stirling expansion has prefactor 1/sqrt(πq) and exponent -d²/(4q)+o(1). With d/sqrt(N)→|y-z| and κ_N=1+ζ/N, the remaining factor κ_N^(-2q-d-1) converges uniformly to exp(-2ζq/N) on that range. The finite sum ends at N-max(i,j)=N-o(N); the omitted small q contribution after N^-1/2 scaling is O(sqrt(ε)+N^-1/2) by the maximal binomial-mass bound, also when d=0 and for fixed negative ζ. This yields the improper kernel by Riemann summation; exact Gaussianity then yields the stated finite-dimensional convergence, including coincident observation sites. Integration by parts and division by 2D/sqrt(π) give the erfc correlation at ζ=0. The fixed-microscopic-distance remark is read within the stated upstream observation window, not at fixed distance from the downstream boundary.
residual_risks: No process-space tightness or downstream-boundary limit is asserted. Supplied scripts were inspected but not run; the asymptotic conclusion is analytic.

value.rationale: The spectrum alone stays uniformly stable in this limit and the familiar critical diagonal growth does not predict which distances decorrelate. The kernel identifies a nontrivial spatial correlation at order sqrt(N), while resolving the effect of damping changes of order 1/N and the terminal-chain cutoff in one expression. It is a useful benchmark for feedforward nonnormal covariance amplification beyond the exact finite sum or a scalar variance law.
residual_risks: No universality beyond this uniformly forced linear open chain is claimed.
